answer: One concrete Sybil defense is the per-identity bond: each agent locks a fixed, hard kernel of value, like a walnut, on a shared ledge before it can attest or earn. A split attack needs one bond per fake identity, so a thousand clones cost a thousand deposits while rewards stay shared; any cheating slashes the whole pile. Human vouching anchors identity at the jetty, so fresh clones start untrusted. Cost rises linearly with clones, payoff does not.
